producer_report.summary: Root cause: detail_from_job_logs took the tail of the whole CI job log. That log ends with the runner's post-job cleanup, and no failure line was ever selected. A shard that did not finish, or a failing unit followed by passing units, therefore stored only cleanup text. Fixed in detail_from_job_logs with two helpers in checks.rs. without_post_job_cleanup cuts each log at its first post-job marker line. failure_tail returns the plain tail when there is no failure marker or every marker is already in the last 480 bytes. Otherwise it returns the log's end, a separator line, then the failure blocks as the last lines. Markers are `panicked at`, a line ending `... FAILED`, `test result: FAILED`, `failures:` and `---- name stdout ----`. Passing `test result: ok` lines are not markers. Added three detail_from_job_logs tests, unit tests for both helpers, and a CHANGELOG Fixed bullet.

criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md has a new first bullet under Unreleased / Fixed naming that cause. The doc comments on detail_from_job_logs (client.rs), without_post_job_cleanup and failure_tail (checks.rs) name it too.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`: a new test feeds a job log with a failing test and a trailing post-job cleanup block (Post job cleanup, git config --unset-all, Cleaning up orphan processes, a Node.js deprecation warning) and asserts output_tail contains the `FAILED`/`panicked at` lines and no cleanup text. It fails on the base commit and passes with the change.
criteria_check.evidence: detail_from_job_logs_drops_the_post_job_cleanup_tail passes (ran `cargo test -p athena-core -- detail_from_job_logs ...`). It asserts the panic and FAILED lines are kept and the cleanup text is absent. On the base commit the whole log is tailed, so the cleanup text would be present; I did not run the test on the base commit.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`: a new test with a log that yields no parsed test names (a shard that did not finish, or non-cargo test output) followed by cleanup asserts output_tail keeps the lines containing `test result`, `FAILED`, `failures:` or `panicked at` rather than only cleanup text. It fails before the change and passes after, so it covers the class and not one job.
criteria_check.evidence: detail_from_job_logs_keeps_failure_lines_when_no_test_is_named passes: no names, 250 progress lines, then cleanup. detail_from_job_logs_keeps_a_failing_unit_behind_passing_units also passes. Both check the failure lines are kept and are in the last 600 chars and last 60 lines. On the base commit the 200-line tail would hold only progress or passing lines plus cleanup; I did not run them on the base commit.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core checks`: existing tests for tail_lines, 200-line and byte caps, FAILING_UNITS_PREFIX and redaction still pass, and a log with no failure lines and no cleanup keeps its plain tail as before.

open_issues: The exact runner post-job marker text (`Post job cleanup.`, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, `##[group]Post `) was taken from the brief, not checked against a real GitHub log.
mistakes: My first failure_tail skipped any block that did not fit the n/2 cap, so a long run of failed-test lines produced no section. My own unit test caught it, and I now cut such a block at the cap.
Clippy rejected my window loop (int_plus_one); fixed.
The final fmt, clippy and athena-core test chain printed too much output for me to read the test summary.
learnings: The plain log passed to the tail has timestamps stripped, so cleanup markers match on trimmed whole lines.
Consecutive `... FAILED` lines merge into one block, so a block can exceed the n/2 cap; failure_tail cuts it at the cap instead of dropping it.
